name: Hoi An
summary: A small riverside trading port, best seen on foot or by bicycle. Mornings in the old town, afternoons at the beach or in the rice fields, and evenings under the lanterns.
seasonNote: October and November bring heavy rain and frequent flooding in the old town.
arrival: Fly or take the train to Da Nang, then 45 minutes by taxi or shuttle.
gettingAround: The old town is closed to cars for much of the day; rent a bicycle for the beach and countryside.
cashTip: Carry dong for street food, markets and old town tickets; tailors and hotels take cards.
foodTip: Try cao lầu noodles, white rose dumplings, cơm gà chicken rice and a bánh mì.
buyTip: Tailored clothes (allow two fittings), silk lanterns and leather goods.
baseArea: Edge of the old town, or An Bang beach
reviewSummary: These places are an editorial shortlist of the sights and food the city is best known for. Popularity numbers come from Wikipedia readership, and from Google Maps once it is connected; places without a number are kept unranked.

items.name: Hoi An Ancient Town
items.summary: A 15th to 19th-century trading port of ochre shophouses, assembly halls and lanterns.
items.expect: A ticket covers five heritage buildings; evenings are crowded.
items.tip: Walk it at 7 am before the groups arrive, then again after dark.

items.name: My Son Sanctuary
items.summary: Brick temple towers of the Cham kingdom in a jungle valley, from the 4th to 13th centuries.
items.expect: Hot by mid-morning; many towers were damaged by bombing.
items.tip: Take a sunrise tour to arrive before the heat and buses.
